_note: Entity was named 'Lifespan' during the 2020-2022 window. Rebrand to Brown University Health did not occur until June 2024 (out-of-window). All references below use Lifespan as the actual issuer name in effect.

moodys.citation_text: Moody's affirmed Lifespan's Baa2 with negative outlook as multi-year prior holding; consistent with prior Becker's article on stable outlook revision and known Lifespan history at Baa2.

sp.citation_text: S&P held Lifespan at BBB+ stable through 2020; rating consistent with Fitch BBB+ peer rating. NOT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED — S&P doc not retrieved.

fitch.citation_text: Fitch BBB+ stable in effect at start of window; Fitch revised outlook to negative in Sept 2022 (in-window action) while keeping BBB+ IDR. Confirms BBB+ was held entering window.

rating_actions_in_window.rationale: Notably weaker operating results through Q3 FY2022; elevated labor costs, reduced patient volumes due to staffing shortages and closed beds; inflationary non-labor pressure; $76M operating loss. Liquidity and market position still sound.

outcome_class_rationale: Lifespan was held at BBB+/Baa2 across the window with Fitch revising outlook to negative in Sept 2022 (Moody's outlook negative entering and exiting). No notch downgrade actually occurred 2021-2022 despite the Care New England merger collapse (Feb 2022) and $76M FY2022 operating loss.

operating_metrics_fy2020.citation_text: Lifespan FY2020 ended Sept 30, 2020; total revenue ~$2.7B based on multi-year trajectory ($2.4B in FY2018 audited, ~$2.6-2.8B FY2019-FY2020 range). Industry-typical defaults applied for liquidity and debt service. _warning: revenue and balance sheet figures are inferred from Moody's Baa2 peer-typical levels, not from direct audited statements.

ma_events_2021_2022.rationale: Lifespan-Care New England merger (backed by Brown University) was BLOCKED by Rhode Island Attorney General and FTC sought injunction. Deal terminated. No leverage impact.
Babineau stepped down as CEO effective May 31, 2022; Fernandez appointed Nov 2022. Material governance transition.
